title: Enterobacter cloacae cystitis on ceftriaxone, no fever or upper tract signs, nothing by mouth

provenance.author: Claude Code (draft for owner review), case list approved by the owner

clinical_review.notes: Changed in #212 (AmpC at every site, owner decision 2026-11-21); awaiting owner review.

story: A 74-year-old woman on postoperative day 2 after hip fracture repair develops dysuria and frequency without fever, flank pain or bacteremia; she has no indwelling urinary catheter. She has an ileus and takes nothing by mouth. Urine grows Enterobacter cloacae complex, resistant to the usual oral agents; she is on IV ceftriaxone.

problems.title: Closed fracture of the femoral neck

expected_findings.summary: Enterobacter cloacae complex cystitis on ceftriaxone: generally avoided for an inducible AmpC organism even when susceptible; the preferred agents (nitrofurantoin, TMP-SMX) are not active here, so a single dose of an aminoglycoside or renally adjusted cefepime are the alternatives.

reference_answer: Flag ceftriaxone. IDSA 2026 suggests generally avoiding third-generation cephalosporins for Enterobacter cloacae complex even when susceptible. Its preferred agents for AmpC cystitis, nitrofurantoin and TMP-SMX, test resistant, and she takes nothing by mouth. Suggest a single dose of gentamicin (5 mg/kg IV, adjusted body weight if obese; avoid with hearing loss or significant renal impairment) or cefepime adjusted for her creatinine clearance (check weight; Cockcroft-Gault likely under 60 mL/min at 74). Completing ceftriaxone may be reasonable only if it was started empirically, she is clearly improving and no catheter or other source persists; repeat the urine culture if symptoms persist. Confirm she has urinary symptoms (otherwise this is asymptomatic bacteriuria and needs no antibiotic) and no indwelling catheter. Total 3 to 7 days for cystitis, counting the ceftriaxone days, or one gentamicin dose.
rationale: Changed from a negative control in #212 (owner decision, 2026-11-21, after an OpenEvidence answer on this case): ceftriaxone is not preferred even for bladder-limited cystitis with an inducible AmpC organism, so the AmpC rule now fires at every site with site-specific alternatives. The case id keeps its original name because the chart, photograph and recorded FHIR fixture are keyed on it. IV to PO does not apply: she is not taking anything by mouth and no susceptible oral agent exists.

citations.supports: AmpC-producing Enterobacterales: ceftriaxone for uncomplicated cystitis versus invasive infections; cefepime when the MIC is 2 or lower.
Prospective audit and feedback of antibiotic therapy as a stewardship intervention.

Question 2.4, read in IDSA's published 2026 text 2026-11-21: "the panel suggests generally avoiding third-generation cephalosporins" for moderate-risk AmpC organisms, and ceftriaxone "is not suggested for the treatment of invasive infections"; continuing an empirically started course may be reasonable in a non-severe infection with improvement and source control. The section does not define invasive or mention pyelonephritis or cystitis.
